questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, highlighters, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.

What is an internal diseconomy of scale that often arises as a firm becomes larger?

options.A: a more complex decision-making process
options.B: an increase in the cost of raising finance for investment
options.C: an increase in traffic congestion
options.D: upward pressure on wages in the local labour market

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a firm’s cost and revenue curves. MC cost, AC revenue MR AR O output The firm changes its objective from profit maximisation to sales revenue maximisation. Which groups are likely to be winners and losers as a result of this change? winners losers

options.A: customers shareholders
options.B: managers customers
options.C: workers managers
options.D: shareholders workers

questions.questionText: The table shows some of the assumptions of perfect competition and monopolistic competition. Which pairing is correct? perfect competition monopolistic competition

options.A: barriers to entry small number of firms
options.B: differentiated products large number of firms
options.C: freedom of entry and exit barriers to entry
options.D: large number of firms differentiated products

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the initial cost and revenue curves of a profit-maximising monopolist. MC costs, revenue P AR MR O J K output What would cause the firm to increase its output from OJ to OK?

options.A: The government fixes the price at OP.
options.B: The government requires the firm to charge a price equal to marginal cost.
options.C: The government imposes an indirect tax on the firm’s product.
options.D: The firm is allowed to earn only a normal profit.

questions.questionText: What makes it most likely that a firm’s profits will be volatile and subject to substantial fluctuations?

options.A: Fixed costs are a high percentage of total costs.
options.B: It produces a diversified range of products.
options.C: It produces basic consumer products.
options.D: It sells its product in a number of different markets.

questions.questionText: A country has a negative income tax. The curve NT in the diagram shows the country’s initial tax schedule. + NT tax NT O income –

options.A: strengthen more equal
options.B: strengthen less equal
options.C: weaken less equal
options.D: weaken more equal

questions.questionText: What is most likely to contribute to households finding themselves in a poverty trap?

options.A: means-tested benefits
options.B: progressive taxation
options.C: regressive taxation
options.D: universal benefits

questions.questionText: The firms in a perfectly competitive industry combine to form a monopoly. What would prevent a deadweight welfare loss resulting?

options.A: The government imposes an indirect tax on the monopolist’s product.
options.B: The government requires the monopolist to charge a price equal to average cost.
options.C: The monopolist adopts marginal cost pricing.
options.D: The monopolist charges the same price to all consumers.

questions.questionText: What might cause the growth of measured GNP to overstate the ‘true’ rate of economic growth in an economy?

options.A: People move from unpaid housework to paid employment.
options.B: The exchange rate is overvalued according to purchasing power parity.
options.C: There is a reduction in environmental pollution.
options.D: There is a reduction in the rate of investment in physical capital.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows changes in broad and narrow measures of money supply between 2004 and 2006. narrow money % key –3 2004 2005 2006 Euro area Britain broad money Japan
Which assertion could be described as monetarist rather than Keynesian?

options.A: The interest elasticity of investment expenditure is close to zero.
options.B: The money supply is the main determinant of aggregate monetary expenditure.
options.C: The money supply is the main determinant of output in the long-run.
options.D: The velocity of circulation of money is unstable over time.

questions.questionText: In an economy, the marginal propensity to consume of the unemployed is higher than that of taxpayers. The government increases expenditure on unemployment benefits by $10m and increases taxation by $10million. What will be the impact on aggregate demand?

options.A: It will be unchanged.
options.B: It will increase by less than $10 million.
options.C: It will increase by $10 million.
options.D: It will decrease by $10 million.

questions.questionText: According to loanable funds theory, what will cause the rate of interest to rise?

options.A: a decrease in the demand for money
options.B: an increase in the level of savings
options.C: an increase in the rate of investment
options.D: an increase in the supply of money

questions.questionText: What is most likely to contribute to high long-term growth rates of GNP per head?

options.A: government imposition of maximum prices for particular goods
options.B: high rates of trade union membership amongst the labour force
options.C: high ratios of saving to GNP
options.D: restrictions on inward foreign investment

questions.questionText: A country experiences cyclical unemployment due to a decrease in domestic spending. If the government takes no action in response, what will be a likely consequence?

options.A: an increase in the current account deficit on the balance of payments
options.B: an increase in the government’s budget deficit
options.C: an increase in the rate of inflation
options.D: an increase in the volume of investment

questions.questionText: What is a possible combination of a cost and a benefit of rising levels of unemployment? cost benefit

options.A: a deterioration in human capital an increase in capital expenditure
options.B: an increase in import expenditure a decrease in government tax revenue
options.C: an increase in the rate of economic growth a more responsive workforce
options.D: an irretrievable loss of output a reduction in inflationary pressure

questions.questionText: What would increase an economy’s actual output but not its potential output?

options.A: an increase in the capital available to the labour force
options.B: an increase in the labour force’s skill level
options.C: an increase in the number in the labour force
options.D: an increase in the proportion of the labour force employed

questions.questionText: Which combination indicates that a country is operating a ‘dirty float’? nominal exchange rate foreign currency reserves

options.A: depreciates by 20% decrease by $1 billion
options.B: depreciates by 20% unchanged
options.C: unchanged decrease by $1 billion
options.D: unchanged unchanged

questions.questionText: What is a reflationary fiscal measure?

options.A: reducing interest rates
options.B: increasing the money supply
options.C: increasing taxes
options.D: increasing government spending

questions.questionText: A country’s government wishes to switch demand away from private consumption towards investment and net exports. Which combination of policy measures would be most likely to help it achieve this objective? rate of value interest rates added tax

options.A: decrease decrease
options.B: decrease increase
options.C: increase decrease
options.D: increase increase

questions.questionText: A government aims to achieve steady and stable growth, in line with the economy’s long-run increase in productivity. If this objective is achieved, how is this likely to affect average living standards and the level of unemployment? average living level of standards unemployment

options.A: constant falling
options.B: falling unchanged
options.C: rising rising
options.D: rising unchanged

questions.questionText: During year 1, a government announces a temporary one-year reduction in the level of indirect taxation balanced by an equivalent temporary one-year increase in direct taxation. What is most likely to be the impact on household saving in year 1 and in year 2? impact on household impact on household saving in year 1 saving in year 2

options.A: decrease decrease
